name: Calcol
interpretive_note: Scripture places Calcol among the "sons of Zerah" in Judah's genealogy (1 Chronicles 2:6), which would put him in the generation just after Jacob's sons, yet 1 Kings 4:31 invokes his wisdom as a living point of comparison for Solomon centuries later, calling the same group "sons of Mahol." Whether these are the same men, remembered across many generations (since "son of" can mean "descendant of" in genealogies), or whether 1 Kings 4:31 names different, closer-to-Solomon's-day individuals who merely share these names, is debated; Scripture does not resolve the question.
source_summary: A son of Zerah in Judah's genealogy remembered as one of the proverbially wise men of Israel's early history, named in 1 Kings 4:31 as part of the standard by which Solomon's God-given wisdom was measured and shown to surpass.
family_friendly_summary: Calcol was known in Israel's history as a very wise man. He is named in the Bible as one of the wisest men of his time, alongside three other men named Ethan, Heman, and Darda. We don't know exactly what wise things Calcol said or did -- the Bible only tells us he was famous for his wisdom. Later, when the Bible wants to describe just how wise King Solomon was, it says Solomon was even wiser than Calcol and these other well-known wise men. That shows just how amazing God's gift of wisdom to Solomon really was.
adult_story: Calcol is named in Scripture only as a byword for wisdom. Among the Judahites descended from Zerah (Judah's son by Tamar) was "Calcol," listed alongside his brothers Zimri, Ethan, Heman, and Dara (1 Chronicles 2:6). First Kings 4:29-31 praises Solomon's God-given wisdom by comparison, saying Solomon "was wiser than all men, than Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Calcol and Darda, the sons of Mahol" -- implying that these four were already renowned sages of Israel's history whose reputation for wisdom was proverbial enough that surpassing them meant something. (Whether "the sons of Mahol" of 1 Kings 4:31 are the same men as the "sons of Zerah" of 1 Chronicles 2:6 is debated among scholars, since Scripture does not explicitly equate the two lists.) Nothing else is recorded of Calcol's words, deeds, or the content of his wisdom -- only that his name had become a standard other wise men, even a king as wise as Solomon, could be measured against.
